evidence: src/presentation/controllers/StockController.ts: constructor(private readonly receiving: ReceivingService, private readonly counts: CycleCountService) injects business-layer services, which this layer is allowed to depend on (dependency wiring)
receive(dto: ReceiveDto) passes dto fields to this.receiving.receive(...) and maps the result to { bin: bin.code, quantity: bin.quantity }, which is response mapping
pick(dto: PickDto) returns this.receiving.pick(dto.sku, dto.quantity) as is, so the reorder decision is made by the business service
count(dto: CountDto) maps the service result to { ok: d === null, delta: d?.delta ?? 0 }, which reshapes the response and is not a domain calculation
The DTOs come from '../dto/requests', which belongs to the presentation layer
parsedVerdict.reasoning: StockController.ts is a presentation file, and everything in it fits that role. Its constructor takes ReceivingService and CycleCountService from the business layer, which presentation is allowed to depend on, so that is ordinary dependency wiring. Each method takes a request DTO declared in this project's presentation layer, makes one call to a business service, and turns the result into a response shape. The only logic it adds is in count(): `ok: d === null, delta: d?.delta ?? 0`, which reshapes the service's result for the response. It doesn't calculate a delta, decide on reordering or check an invariant. Those decisions stay in the business services: pick() returns the service's `reorder` flag unchanged.
